title: One curve, two stories
hook: A change in a count can have more than one explanation.

knows: Animals interact with other organisms and their surroundings.
doesNotKnow: A toy prey count falls over two years. One story says predators increased; another says food decreased. Does the prey curve alone distinguish the stories?

misconception: One observation or model rule gives a complete answer about nature.
objective: A toy prey count falls over two years. One story says predators increased; another says food decreased. Does the prey curve alone distinguish the stories?

claims.text: A toy prey count falls over two years. One story says predators increased; another says food decreased. Does the prey curve alone distinguish the stories? Both panels show the same stipulated prey-count decline alongside different proposed explanations. The curve alone does not decide between them; data on predators, food and other factors would help.
claims.source: Unverified reference lead for independent check: OpenStax Biology 2e, ecology and populations, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e . Exact claim-specific sources have not been verified.

claims.text: The panels depict a simplified illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
A bird count declines and two hypotheses could explain it. Does the count alone establish which hypothesis caused it? A compatible pattern is not enough to distinguish multiple explanations.
